claims.text: The equiatomic Ti20Ni20Co20Cr20Fe20 alloy can be prepared in a single-phase solid-solution state.
The intervention consists of pack-cementation aluminizing at 900°C for 4 hours followed by oxidation at 950°C for 30 minutes.
The specified treatment will form a uniform, thin, adherent Al2O3 surface scale.
The specified treatment will produce a gradual subsurface diffusion-gradient layer.
The Al2O3 scale acts as an oxidation barrier.
The Al2O3 scale prevents rapid external degradation during high-temperature exposure.
The diffusion-gradient layer enhances load transfer.
The diffusion-gradient layer reduces surface crack initiation.
The Al2O3 scale and diffusion-gradient layer together retain mechanical integrity during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The coated alloy will have statistically significantly better oxidation resistance than the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will have statistically significantly higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will have statistically significantly better elevated-temperature creep resistance than the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will have statistically significantly longer elevated-temperature fatigue life than the uncoated alloy.
The hypothesis is applicable when the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution and is tested in an oxidizing environment from 600°C to 800°C.
Departures from the specified treatment temperatures or exposure conditions may compromise coating effectiveness.
Long-term Al2O3-scale durability under cyclic or dynamic loading may be limited by interfacial adhesion and residual stresses.
